english_verification.review_scope: Read representative local history, the formation-decision branch, current English country localisations for both F38 and F97, and narrative terms for the canals, Golden Highway, Phoenix Crown, and local administration. Read actual fixed-revision Wiki chunks covering the 1162 disestablishment label and the 1161–1169 war and 1170 Kalib Assembly. This was not a full mission-tree audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Phoenix Empire page labels the end as 1162 (Jexis's assassination); the First Cinder War account describes fighting through 1169 and dissolution at the 1170 Kalib Assembly. Both source accounts remain distinct.

The Mod's F38 and F97 country files have different internal filenames, but current English and Chinese country localisations display Phoenix Empire for both; the Tags remain distinct, with F97 the West Cannor-capital variant.
The full reachability of timed missions, predecessor mission retention, and optimal routing was not tested in-game.

rationale.campaign_length: 49 Phoenix Empire-specific mission definitions; predecessor missions are counted separately, and the objectives span multiple continents.
rationale.colonization: The 49 dedicated missions focus mainly on conquest and development across the Old World, not overseas colonization.
rationale.complexity: Formation requirements, timed missions, intercontinental truces, overextension, subjects, and palace construction all compete for attention.
rationale.dark_story: Public works and acceptance of multiple cultures coexist with forced religious uniformity and a narrative of crushing resistance.
rationale.difficulty: Planning is demanding beyond military strength: ten timely mission completions and imperial administration matter; difficulty was not quantified in-game.
rationale.diplomacy: Integrating subjects, protectorates, and local administration matter, though warfare remains the main driver of progress.
rationale.early_pressure: Timed objectives begin immediately after formation; pressure during the pre-formation stage in 1444 depends on the chosen predecessor.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Sun Worship and magical laws matter to the narrative, but the campaign plays chiefly through military, government, faith, and infrastructure.
rationale.narrative_density: Jaher and Jexis's imperial legacy, restoration, the Phoenix Crown, and a global Sun Elf empire run through the story.
rationale.tall_play: Farmland, cities, canals, and palace development matter, but mainly as the foundation for a wide empire.
rationale.trade_economy: The Golden Highway, Bulwar canals, the Divenhal Sea, and east–west commerce form the central economic theme.
rationale.warfare: Formation requires consolidating Bulwar; later missions range across Cannor, the Salahad deserts, Rahen, and Haless.

identity.appearance: Not present as a country in 1444: the historical Phoenix Empire has fallen and is restored by a qualifying Sun Elf country through a decision.
identity.formation_scope: Requires a Sun Elf country and ruler culture, Bulwari Sun Worship, and at least 100 provinces in the Bulwar superregion owned directly or by non-sovereign subjects; peace and independence requirements also apply. A capital in West Cannor produces F97, otherwise F38. Both use the same Phoenix missions; countries previously tagged F52 are excluded from that mission group.
predecessors: Any Sun Elf country meeting the general decision requirements; Birzartanšes (F21) is one possible predecessor, not the only one.
identity.region: Bulwar → Cannor / Rahen / Haless (origin in Bulwar, with intercontinental expansion)

survey_region.note: Ranking-table row 177 corresponds to Phoenix Empire. The production entry records both F38 and the West Cannor-capital variant F97; both Tags use this same source row.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
"The conqueror stood at the world far edge and stared across the sunlit sea,
And felt aught but crushing darkness, No thrill of victory.
His blood sang for conquest but the world had struck him lame,
And he wept great tears of fire and in thundering voice proclaimed.
"I have reached my zenith, the highest I shall mark,
For there are no more worlds to conquer, my soul is torn apart."
He turned to face his empire, resigned to his fate,
Jaher's time had passed, his death he did await.
Till one takes up the mantle.
The Phoenix Crown awaits."
-from the Litany of Jaher by Sarada Razumir

description.text: The Sun Elves have long been styled the Chosen of Surael, destined to pave the way for his glorious return. Yet even as the Empire rose from the ashes of Jexis' reign there was a significant minority within its borders who refused to follow the true faith, not to mention those outside the Empire who still clung to dead gods. To combat this the priests of Surael formed The Order of the Light of Truth to spread the teachings of the Sun Temple to the farthest corners of the world, a task they proved apt in achieving.

description.text: The Phoenix Empire is one of soaring temples and palaces that reach towards the heavens, from the Palace of Eternal Fire to the Dawn temple its lands are filled with wonders undreamed, draped in marble and gold. It is not uncommon for the Elvish nobility to have sprawling estates larger than most towns as they add grander and grander edifices as the centuries wear on. With its resurgence the new Emperors undertook great projects to craft edifices to surpass anything found in the kingdoms of man and cement the glory of a new age of Elven leadership and peace.

description.text:
In years past Jaher and Jexis lead the finest armies that the world has ever seen in their conquests. Legends of endless ranks of Legionaries clad in glittering golden armour and armed with shining silver blades are told across all of Cannor. Since the fall of Jexis the proud warrior traditions of the Phoenix Legions has faded into history and no more golden warriors march across Sarhal for the glory of the Sun Elf people.

Now that our great Empire has been reformed from the ashes, so too must the Legions march. For too long have those blades of legend been left to rust and dull under the weight of years. Once more the Phoenix Legions shall rise and once more the enemies of the Sun Elves shall tremble at their passing.

description.text: Trade is one of the most vital practices in the Empire, much of the Elves' vast wealth is drawn from eastern goods traveling along the Empire's trade routes to be sold in the western lands of Cannor. To facilitate this trade, as well as to give an edge to their own merchant class, the Imperial government set about establishing a series of way stations called The Offices of Trade throughout its vast holdings where their merchants could rest and prepare for long journeys.

description.text: In the imperial capital of Bulwar, near to the Imperial Palace, lies a vast and sprawling complex of gold and lapis lazuli. Its official name is the Imperial Academy of Progress but most know it by another name The Gilded Menagerie. It is here that the future governors of the Empire are trained, many a noble house has sent its scions here in order to gain favour and position within the Imperial Bureaucracy. Its darker purpose is the training ground of the Empire's vast network of spies and assassins. It is said that in every court in Cannor, in every gathering of mages the Menagerie has a dozen sets of ears listening to every word and a dozen sharpened knives at every back.

description.text: The Phoenix Empire and its Sun Elf rulers are masters over vast and diverse lands stretching from horizon to horizon. It is within this Empire more than any other that cultures meet, trade and mingle under the enlightened rule of the chosen. The Sun Elves have accepted their destiny as those who will one day lead the entire world under their glorious rule and accept all the lesser races and accept all into the fold, provided they kneel at the feet of their betters.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you prefer a stable small country, fewer wars, or do not want to manage overextension and timed objectives.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Unify Bulwar as a predecessor and form the empire, then sequence western and eastern campaigns around timed objectives while rebuilding roads, palaces, and imperial infrastructure and managing overextension.
player_overview.overview: The Phoenix Empire is not a 1444 starting country: it is an ancient empire that a Sun Elf state can restore after unifying Bulwar. Once formed, you must repair the Golden Highway and canals, build palaces, and press along the empire's old eastern and western fronts. Its mission tree has 49 dedicated definitions, some of whose expansion objectives count toward the Phoenix Crown only if completed on time. You will manage trade and culturally diverse subjects while facing an intense narrative of religious uniformity.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy long formation campaigns, intercontinental wars, timed route planning, and imperial construction.
signature_features: F38 and the West Cannor-capital variant F97 share the same restoration mission tree.
Ten timely mission completions and ruler requirements turn the Phoenix Crown into a route-planning challenge.
The Golden Highway, capital palace, and Phoenix Estates connect intercontinental conquest to imperial administration.
player_overview.tagline: Restore the Sun Elves' ancient empire, then conquer both ends of the world before time runs out.

reasons: A clear objective: form a historical empire from a local Sun Elf country.
Ten timed objectives and the Phoenix Crown create a distinctive planning challenge.
The Golden Highway, palaces, and estates add a construction layer to expansion.
warnings: Formation requirements are demanding and predecessor campaigns differ.
The late-game conquest footprint is enormous and can become exhausting.
Religious uniformity and coercive imperial rule make the narrative far from gentle.

positive_indicators: Restoring canals and the Golden Highway, and developing cities and farmland.
Accepting multiple Bulwari cultures when the empire is formed.
Newly conquered regions may retain local administration temporarily; mission text rejects enslavement in East Cannor.
values.rationale: The score does not penalize conquest, monarchy, or Sun Elf identity. Canals, farmland, cities, and trade routes bring clear public benefit; the empire accepts several Bulwari cultures and retains some local administration. However, mission text explicitly calls for eliminating heresy and replacing other faiths in Haless, and presents burning resistant settlements and forests as possible means. Recognition is conditional on loyalty to the emperor and Surael, not equal self-determination, so the overall result is dark-leaning Neutral.
red_flags: Mission text calls for eliminating Bulwari heresies and other faiths in Haless.
The eastern campaign describes burning resistant settlements and forests as possible methods.
Local autonomy is conditional on serving imperial control and conquest.
